Explore how outfield fence distance, wall height, and stadium altitude govern home run rates across Major League Baseball.









Statistical Regression Summary

Correlation Coefficient (\(r\)): -0.146 (moderate negative correlation)
Coefficient of Determination (\(R^2\)): 0.021
Regression Equation: HR Factor = -0.42 * (Avg Fence Dist) + 256.0


Key takeaway: Shorter outfield fences strongly facilitate home run production. Each 1-foot decrease in average fence distance correlates with an increase in home run factor.

title: About the MLB Statcast Ballpark Explorer
text:
This project explores how physical ballpark dimensions, wall heights, and environmental factors influence home run rates in Major League Baseball. Built as part of a Bayesian Data Science workflow using R, Quarto, and the tidyverse, the interactive visualizations allow students and analysts to investigate both macro park factors and micro batted-ball metrics.



MLB Baseball Savant: Official Statcast Park Factors and Ballpark Dimensions leaderboard (2018–2026).
Statcast Batted Ball Tracking: Exit velocity (mph), launch angle (degrees), hit distance (ft), and pitch velocity for individual home runs.




A park factor of 100 represents the MLB average baseline:

> 100: The ballpark favors hitters (e.g. 115 indicates a park produces 15% more home runs than a neutral park).
< 100: The ballpark favors pitchers (e.g. 85 indicates a park suppresses home runs by 15%).





Document Publishing: Quarto (.qmd)
Analysis & Modeling: R (tidyverse, jsonlite)
Interactive Visualizations: plotly
Data Tables: DT
Design System: Custom Dark Glassmorphism CSS
